interest: Shows 1940-43 U.S. multinationals (IBM, Paraffine, American Express) navigating Japanese controls, plus State's retaliation debate and Mitsui/NYK shipping intelligence.
overview: Docket sheets for file 894.5034 (Aug 1940-Feb 1943) track American firms (Paraffine, American Express, IBM) facing Japanese controls, Grew and Livesey's debate on retaliatory measures against Japanese holdings, and wartime despatches from Argentina and Sweden on Mitsui Shipping and Nippon Yusen Kaisha.

people.name: Frederick Livesey
people.role: State Department Adviser on International Economic Affairs

subfiles.about: A Department of State docket sheet recording a 1940 communication regarding the Paraffine Companies, Inc.'s interest in a Japanese roofing plant and its desire to sell stock for U.S. dollars.
subfiles.summary: Lists an August 1940 report: Paraffine Companies sought to sell its 60% Japanese roofing-plant stake, with payment guaranteed in dollars.
subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers regarding Japanese Corporations (Sub. No. 22)

subfiles.about: A Non-Jacket Case List of Papers sheet indexing 1941 records on Japanese industrial control legislation, conditions of American businesses, and corporate inquiries.
subfiles.summary: Sheet 4 (1941) lists Grew's telegrams on Japanese industrial controls and retaliation, and Livesey's memos on foreign officer bans.
subfiles.title: Non-Jacket Case List of Papers, Sheet No. 4, regarding Japanese Corporations (Sub. Nos. 23-28)

subfiles.about: A List of Papers sheet indexing 1941-1943 communications regarding IBM interests in Japan and diplomatic reports on Japanese shipping firms.
subfiles.summary: Sheet 5 (1941-43) lists IBM's request to protect its Japanese subsidiary, plus reports on Mitsui Shipping and Nippon Yusen Kaisha.
subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers, Sheet No. 5, regarding Japanese Corporations (Sub. Nos. 29-31)
